newsitem.title: USA: Two bcfd U.S. natgas output shut in by Josephine.
newsitem.headline: Two bcfd U.S. natgas output shut in by Josephine.

text.p: Tropical Storm Josephine, sweeping east-northeast across the U.S. Gulf, has forced natural gas producers to shut in around two billion cubic feet (bcf) a day of output.
But most companies said their precautionary production halts were likely to be lifted soon as the storm passes offshore fields on its way toward the west coast of Florida.
Panenergy Corp said producers on its Texas Eastern and Trunkline pipeline systems shut in about 700 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd).
Most of the gas lost on Texas Eastern was on the Venice system off eastern Louisiana, while the Trunkline cuts came on the Terrebonne system, a spokesman said.
The company was not sure when production would be fully restored.

And Williams Cos unit Transco said about 650 mmcfd had been shut on its system today. But a company spokesman added, "It doesn't look like it's going any higher. It should start to go down as the storm moves farther east."

The specter of tighter supplies helped firm spot gas prices at the U.S. Gulf this morning by five to 10 cents, with some pipes quoted as high as the low-$2.30s per million British thermal units (mmBtu).
ANR Pipeline Co reported it evacuated its High Island Offshore System (HIOS) Block 264 located offshore Texas over the weekend, forcing the shut-in of about 150 mmcfd.
The company said it expected crews to return to the offshore Texas facility later today.

At ANR's Eugene Island Block 188, there were no evacuations, but compressors were shut due to the cuts in production. A company spokesman could not comment on what volumes had been cut on this offshore Louisiana platform.
"Everything should be back to normal by tomorrow," he said.

While producers said they had evacuated some personnel from platforms and cut some output as a precaution against the storm, no damage had been reported and most expected gas to be flowing normally in a day or two.
"We started evacuations yesterday morning, but some of the western (U.S. Gulf) employees are going back today," a Chevron spokeswoman said, adding she was not sure how much gas output was affected.
Anadarko also shut several platforms, mostly in the western Gulf of Mexico, but a spokesman said, "The disruptions have been fairly mild and should only last a couple of days."

At 1100 EDT, Tropical Storm Josephine, with winds rising to 70 mph, was 175 miles south-southwest of Apalachicola, Fla., and moving northeast at 23 mph. Forecasters said it was likely to become a hurricane before landfall in Florida sometime Monday night.
Enron, which operates the Florida Gas Transmission pipeline, said deliveries to the state were "pretty normal".
"Our shippers did lose about 100 million (cfd), much of it from Mobile Bay, but they have been successful in resourcing that," a Florida Gas spokeswoman said.
Marathon said it shut in about 150 mmcfd of gross gas production as personnel were evacuated ahead of the storm but expected most to reopen shortly.
